timing.interpretation: Much smaller session drift than prior Mac measurements, but small candidate changes are comparable with same-code variation. No proof of speedup or equivalence. The two blocks are independent process comparisons, not12 independent binary comparisons.

diagnostic_findings.gc: First timed request in every leg records a GC cycle; first baseline request has approximately61.9 microseconds recorded GC pause. This coincides with a slower request but does not prove GC caused its roughly1.7s excess. Concurrent GC, allocation/scheduler effects and host interference remain unseparated. Candidate first-request GC also occurs, so allocation reduction does not by itself eliminate these cycles.
diagnostic_findings.parallelism: Reported aggregate CPU time divided by wall is about1.99-2.09 despite four configured workers and all observed thread affinities4-7. This is an unresolved execution-shape clue, not proof of quota, scheduler failure or underused hardware. A post-run probe of the SSH scope and parent cgroups reported cpu.max=max and cumulative throttling counters0; actual per-request cgroup snapshots were not collected, so avoid a retrospective quota diagnosis.
diagnostic_findings.io: Measured major faults and read_bytes deltas are zero in inspected/retained request observations; raw values are preserved per request. Model residency and matching work counters are checked.
